question: What limits xs's small-file fresh copies once the receiver's global lock and serial final pass are gone, and what removes the next limit?

nodes.title: Race the receiver-lock branch
nodes.question: Do the lock split and the parallel final pass make small fresh copies faster, and do extra receiving workers now help?
nodes.measure: LK1 on the Mac-mars link: parent 21ae6844 against 4c5c425c (engine/receiver-locks), default, --no-atomic and -j8; small-flat, small-deep, real-congress; fresh and no-op; time to durable, 8 blocks.
nodes.hypothesis: N3 small-flat: the transfer phase stayed at 2.96-3.23 s from 1 to 16 receiving workers while their summed write time rose from 2.9 to 47 s. The serial final pass took 1.31-1.45 s of every small-deep run.
nodes.decision: A1: faster: merge it. fresh 0.411 (faster) / noop 1.007 (inconclusive). The receiver-lock branch (c5b765eb54fc against b02ae2394a86) is clearly faster on fresh copies: 'fresh 0.411 (faster)' with a 95% interval of 0.406 to 0.415 over 8 blocks. That is the minimum block count, but the interval is narrow and far below 1. No-op re-syncs are unchanged within noise: 'noop 1.007 (inconclusive)', interval 0.962 to 1.055. Keep it and merge. The pooled verdicts do not separate the default, --no-atomic and -j8 configurations, so whether extra receiving workers now help is not answered by these facts; A2 should look at that split.

nodes.title: Find the next limit
nodes.question: How far is xs from the receiver creating the same files by itself, and what is it doing with the difference?
nodes.measure: The best arm so far against local tar extraction on the receiver (P2b's local arms; mars now runs macOS, so measured again there), and a profile of both ends during a small-deep fresh copy: sample on macOS, perf on Linux. A quiet sender first: P2b lost runs to its load.
nodes.hypothesis: P2b, with mars on Linux: 4 local tar processes took 2.70 s on small-deep (about 37k files/s) against 5.26 s for xs in N3.
nodes.decision: A2: raced: no verdict; no usable decision

nodes.hypothesis: The receiver is close to its disk; small fresh copies are done.

nodes.title: Cheaper destination path walks
nodes.question: Do retained parent descriptors, and single-call opens on Linux, remove the path-walk cost?
nodes.measure: engine/dest-anchors (e51c1df1) on every receiver, and openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH on Linux receivers only; opens per file and time to durable.
nodes.hypothesis: MA7, the Mac receiving a psample pull: most of 187 s of kernel time was openat from the destination path walk. dest-anchors cut those samples by 68%.
Adopt, then find the next limit again (A2).
Not the limit: drop the change.

nodes.title: Fast path for fresh subtrees
nodes.question: Can directories the receiver lacks skip the directory-by-directory request round trip, and the rename per file?
nodes.measure: A new feature bit: listing and data stream together for new directories, NEED frames batched across directories, and optionally one staging directory renamed into place. small-deep and real-congress fresh: time to durable and receiver context switches.
nodes.hypothesis: About 200k voluntary context switches on the receiver per small-deep run; the temporary-file rename cost about 12 us of serialized time per file in N3.
Adopt behind the feature bit, then find the next limit again (A2).

nodes.title: Several receiver processes
nodes.question: Once one process is the limit, do lanes split by top-level subtree scale?
nodes.measure: N TCP streams, each feeding its own receiver process: 1, 2, 4 and 8 lanes into mars (macOS), freya (ZFS) and the Pi (ext4); small-flat, small-deep, real-congress.
nodes.hypothesis: The old xsync gained 1.12-2.18x with streams on Linux receivers and lost 1.12-1.17x on NTFS, where siblings were split across processes.
Adopt lanes, chosen from the core count.

nodes.title: Writeback control
nodes.question: Does starting writeback early shorten the time to durable?
nodes.measure: Linux receivers only: sync_file_range as each file closes, then one syncfs. mars runs macOS, so on the Mac-mars link this node is dropped, not measured.
nodes.hypothesis: P2b's eager-writeback arm was about 1.15x overall; it removed dirty-page throttling stalls such as one block's 56.6 s of receiver write time.
